question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2x-3}}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2x-3}}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2y-3}}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2y-3}} \\ \sqrt[3]{2y-3} & =\frac{2}{x} \\ {(\sqrt[3]{2y-3})}^{3} & ={(\frac{2}{x})}^{3} \\ 2y-3 & =\frac{8}{{x}^{3}} \\ 2y & =\frac{8}{{x}^{3}}+3 \\ y & =\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{3}{2}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x\ne \frac{3}{2},\,f(x)\ne 0.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x\ne 0,\,{f}^{-1}(x)\ne \frac{3}{2}.
$$
